items.title: Arnold Loyacano Interview, 1956-09-29
items.q: The reason for the New York fiasco and for ever leaving the Lambs was a fella named Harry Fitzgerald, a big booking agent from New York came there and he told us how swell the band was and everything.

ctx.x: No. Well, then how come you all left Lambs? Well, how long we had Lambs? Do you remember that?

Well, we started there on, uh, May 18th, 1915. And we were in New York in September. The reason for the New York fiasco and for ever leaving the Lambs was a fella named Harry Fitzgerald, a big booking agent from New York came there and he told us how swell the band was and everything. And he'd, uh, give us a world of the fence around it and didn't even see the fence. There's another guy I didn't sign a contract with. They did, but not me. I told him, no, I want to see this. I said, I want to see the money. Well,…
You mean the band? Yeah, the whole outfit. Well, who'd they take on base? And if you didn't go?
